01 / 12

BEN Engine, Business Edge Node

A family of modular data centers built in off-the-shelf containers and cabinets, with Schreiber AI's controls, twin and commissioning layer.

  • BEN Micro 2–5 kW · BEN 10 10–30 kW · BEN 20 50–150 kW · BEN 40 150–500 kW
  • Modules: Power, Cooling, Compute, Controls; buy one or all
  • Mission profiles set class, redundancy, climate, compliance pack and the risk list

Speaker notes

Audience: engineers, integrators, facilities leads. Set expectations: every number on these slides comes from code in the repository and the evidence file is docs/VALIDATION.md.

02 / 12

A concrete scenario

A regional clinic wants inference on patient data on-site: healthcare profile, 2N power, A1 class, generator standard.

  • Selector: BEN 20, healthcare, hot/humid climate
  • Output: 480 V service size, UPS kVA, battery kWh under the NFPA 855 threshold, cooling units derated for 38 °C design day
  • Proposal, drawings, compliance pack and risk disclosure generated from that configuration

Speaker notes

Walk the selector live on the product page (web/index.html) or the dashboard. Show the validation error path by setting racks to 1 at 150 kW.

03 / 12

One configuration drives everything

config.py is the base model: sizing rules, validation, presets. Downstream generators consume it.

  • BOM with price-confidence split (bom.py + parts_catalog.json)
  • IFC drawing set with CTQ/CTP tables (design/drawings)
  • Twin, CFD, sweeps, commissioning (software/ben_engine)
  • Dashboard 3-D scene and product page selector (JS port with a parity test)

Speaker notes

Mention the parity test: tests/test_selector_parity.py runs node against the Python model so the website cannot drift from engineering.

04 / 12

The digital twin

Lumped thermal and power-chain model with faults, alarms and sensor specs; fit-able from commissioning data.

  • Faults: cooling unit fail, utility loss, door open, filter clog, leak, sensor drift, generator fail
  • Alarms follow ASHRAE class limits of the profile
  • analysis.py fits recirculation, bypass, thermal mass from a load step and predicts with 95 % intervals

Speaker notes

Caveat: thermal masses are design values until measured. The fitter flags envelope UA as weakly identifiable from indoor data; say so.

05 / 12

CFD for layout, not for absolute numbers

2-D lattice-Boltzmann airflow with heat and tracer transport runs per tier in seconds.

  • BEN 20 grid 232 × 90 at 25 mm, 14.6 s runtime
  • Containment closed and supply > demand: recirculation about 0; fan turn-down to 0.9 or a failed unit: 30–40 % recirculation at the end racks
  • Recirculation profile feeds the twin per rack

Speaker notes

Reynolds number in the lattice is ~70 versus ~1e5 real; it is a relative tool for ranking layouts and scenario deltas. The 3-D CFD is on the roadmap after lighthouse data exists.

06 / 12

Measurement plan and calibration

Sensors chosen for the quantities we predict, with uncertainty budgets, tares and placement effects.

  • Rack inlets at 0.4 / 1.2 / 1.8 m, probes 50 mm off perforated doors
  • Differential pressure tared with fans off; taps away from fan discharge
  • GUM budgets: DS18B20 ±0.17 K, SHT45 ±0.14 K, SDP810 ±0.46 Pa at 12 Pa, 4–20 mA loop ±0.025 mA (computed)

Speaker notes

Two budget claims in PROTOCOL.md were not met by the computed budgets (RH and dP); they are left as findings in docs/ANALYSIS_AND_CALIBRATION.md rather than quietly edited.

07 / 12

Controls: open, local-first, hardwired life safety

Raspberry Pi 5 gateway, ESP32 PoE nodes, MQTT/JSON, Modbus/SNMP to third-party gear.

  • Firmware: 37 host unit tests pass; telemetry JSON byte-exact to the protocol spec; 1 h ring buffer and failsafe outputs
  • ESP32 cross-build defined but not run here (toolchain download blocked)
  • IEC 62443 zones; no internet dependency; signed OTA procedure documented

Speaker notes

Be precise: the ESP32 HAL has never been compiled against the real libraries. First pio run on hardware will need fixes. Everything platform-independent is tested.

08 / 12

Build it with workers who have minimal experience

Assembly instructions in ASD-STE100 with hold points for licensed trades, QC forms and CTQ/CTP references.

  • Receiving → container prep (welder hold point) → envelope → fit-out → electrical (licensed) → cooling (licensed) → controls → fire (certified) → FAT → transport → site → SAT
  • 0 instructions over 20 words; banned-word check passes
  • Concept renders per stage, generated from the configuration

Speaker notes

Renders are labelled concept renders. The interference checks table in design/drawings/INTERFERENCE_CHECKS.md is worth showing to engineers: it is what changed the cooling defaults.

09 / 12

Commissioning: the same script in the factory and on site

Ten steps, pass/fail per step, CSV with SHA-256, signature block; the customer can run it.

  • Sensor sanity, I/O point-to-point, meter vs PDU reconciliation, sequential cooling start and failover, load step, ride-through, alarm verification, export
  • BEN 20 simulation: all 10 pass; ride-through 2.1 min to ASHRAE A2 max, UPS empty at 11.8 min

Speaker notes

Run it live: PYTHONPATH=software python -m ben_engine.commissioning --sim --tier ben20 --yes --out /tmp/r.md. Show the report.

10 / 12

Compliance findings that changed the design

A2L refrigerant charge limits, NFPA 855 at 20 kWh, NEC 110.26 vestibule, container as Group U structure.

  • In-row DX specified with R-513A/R-515B
  • Battery energy capped under 20 kWh on Micro/10/20 by default
  • Electrical vestibule on 480 V tiers; second egress door at ≥1000 A frames on BEN 40
  • CSC re-certification after modification; PE-stamped anchorage per climate wind speed

Speaker notes

docs/COMPLIANCE.md section 0 lists these with the calculation basis and what could not be verified (NFPA 76 edition, ASHRAE 15/34 2025).

11 / 12

Validation summary

Verified in simulation and on host; unverified on hardware; least accurate items named.

  • Python suite and firmware host tests pass; Playwright e2e exercises the dashboard
  • Unverified: ESP32 build, gateway on Pi, any physical behaviour
  • Least accurate: ride-through minutes, envelope UA, CFD absolutes, estimate-status prices

Speaker notes

Read docs/VALIDATION.md before presenting; update numbers to the latest run.

12 / 12

Get started

Clone, install, test, run the dashboard, generate a proposal.

  • pip install -r requirements.txt
  • PYTHONPATH=software pytest tests -q --ignore=tests/e2e
  • bash scripts/run_dashboard.sh → http://localhost:8080
  • PYTHONPATH=software python -m ben_engine.proposal --tier ben20 --profile healthcare --out /tmp/p.md
